meta.description: Quote Investigator traces this line to Liane Cordes's 1981 book The Reflecting Pond, not Winston Churchill. Churchill scholars list it as unattributed.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Continuous Effort — Not Strength or Intelligence — Is the Key to Unlocking and Using Our Potential'?
meta.ogDescription: Not Churchill. The line first appears in Liane Cordes's 1981 meditation book The Reflecting Pond; the Churchill credit shows up only by 2001.

answer.label: Not Winston Churchill — actually Liane Cordes
answer.authorDates: American meditation writer · author of “The Reflecting Pond” (Hazelden, 1981)
answer.sourceLine: This exact longer wording — the version with “and using” still in it — is the original. Quote Investigator locates it at page 89 of Liane Cordes’s 1981 Hazelden meditation book The Reflecting Pond: Meditations for Self-Discovery ↗, and finds no substantive support for Churchill, who is not credited with it in Churchill by Himself, the standard collection of his quotations.

source.excerpt: Continuous effort — not strength or intelligence — is the key to unlocking and using our potential.
trail: 1981 — the sentence appears, in full, in The Reflecting Pond: Meditations for Self-Discovery by Liane Cordes, published by Hazelden of Center City, Minnesota; Quote Investigator cites it at page 89 ↗.

1986 — the Fitzhenry & Whiteside Book of Quotations reprints it two words shorter, as “unlocking our potential,” and credits “Liane Cardes”; QI follows that misspelling forward into a 2003 syndicated column ↗.

2001 — the first Churchill ascription in QI’s chronology: the Palm Beach Post of 10 September 2001 runs a lightly reworded version over his name, and Donald J. Trump’s 2004 Trump: How to Get Rich prints it as Churchill’s at page 77 ↗.

Churchill’s own scholars say no — the International Churchill Society’s red-herring article files a short form as “No attribution found” ↗, and Richard Langworth’s list has it twice, under Effort and Persistence.
source.excerptNote: This is the sentence as Quote Investigator reproduces it from the 1981 book. The surrounding meditation on page 89 is not reproduced here — the book is still in copyright, and no public full-text search of it was available to confirm the neighbouring lines.

author.name: Liane Cordes
author.heading: Who was Liane Cordes?
author.metaLine: American meditation writer · The Reflecting Pond (Hazelden, 1981)
author.bio: Liane Cordes wrote The Reflecting Pond: Meditations for Self-Discovery, published in 1981 by Hazelden, the Minnesota publisher whose list serves people in addiction recovery and aftercare. The book is a set of short meditations arranged by subject — self-acceptance, fear, friendship, love — and it is the work she is known for; almost nothing else about her is on the public record, and no life dates are documented. The sentence the internet gives to Churchill is hers, written for readers doing slow, unglamorous, day-by-day work on themselves.

misattribution.heading: What went wrong on the way here
misattribution.intro: Two separate errors ride on this sentence: the wrong author, and — in the version most people see — the wrong words. Both are documented.

items.why: Churchill’s own editor, Richard Langworth, lists the line twice among quotations Churchill never said — under “Effort” and under “Persistence,” both marked “No attribution” ↗ — and the International Churchill Society’s red-herring article calls a short form of it “No attribution found.” It is absent from Churchill by Himself, the standard collection Langworth edited.
A 1986 quotation compendium credited “Liane Cardes” rather than Cordes; Quote Investigator judges this a simple spelling error and tracks it still circulating in a 2003 syndicated column ↗.

The same 1986 compendium printed the line without “and using,” and that trimmed form is the one that spread — including in the 2001 newspaper item and the 2004 Trump business book that QI cites as early Churchill ascriptions ↗. Cordes’s published sentence is the longer one.

misattribution.truthLine: Credit Liane Cordes, The Reflecting Pond: Meditations for Self-Discovery (Hazelden, 1981), page 89 ↗ — and use her full wording, with “and using” left in.

context.heading: How a recovery meditation became a Churchillism
lead: The line was written for a very specific reader. Hazelden is the publisher attached to the Minnesota model of addiction treatment, and The Reflecting Pond is a book of short meditations for people doing aftercare — one subject per chapter, no heroics. Read in that setting, the sentence is not a leadership aphorism at all: it is reassurance that you do not need to be strong or clever to get better, only to keep going.

Detached from the book, it reads like a maxim, and a maxim wants a famous mouth. Two things helped it find one. In 1986 a quotation compendium reprinted the line two words shorter and misspelled the author as “Cardes” — and Quote Investigator notes that Cordes and Churchill sit close together in an alphabetical list of sources ↗, a known mechanism for this kind of slippage. And the sentiment is pure Churchillian archetype: endurance, stubbornness, keeping on. By 2001 a newspaper was printing it over his name, and by 2004 it was in a Donald Trump business book as Churchill’s.
context.detailsSummary: Two wordings, and which one is the original
detailsBody: The version Cordes published in 1981 is the longer one: “Continuous effort — not strength or intelligence — is the key to unlocking and using our potential.” The version that circulates today, on posters and quote sites and in Churchill’s name, is the trimmed one that first appeared in a 1986 compilation, with “and using” removed.

So the popular Churchill quotation is doubly wrong: wrong author, and not even the author’s own sentence. Richard Langworth records the trimmed form as “No attribution,” reported in Investor’s Business Daily in August 2008 ↗.
context.pull: A meditation written for people in recovery became a boardroom Churchillism.

sourcesVerified.claim: Quote Investigator traces the earliest known version, "Continuous effort — not strength or intelligence — is the key to unlocking and using our potential," to Liane Cordes's 1981 book The Reflecting Pond: Meditations for Self-Discovery, quote page 89, Hazelden Publishing, Center City, Minnesota; and states the saying is not listed in Churchill by Himself and has no substantive support connecting it to Churchill.

Quote Investigator documents that the 1986 Fitzhenry & Whiteside Book of Quotations printed the saying with two words deleted and shifted the ascription from "Liane Cordes" to "Liane Cardes" (a probable spelling error), and that the "Liane Cardes" credit was still being propagated by a Copley News Service column dated 1 December 2003.

Quote Investigator's earliest cited Churchill ascription is the Palm Beach Post of 10 September 2001, which printed "A continuous effort, not strength or intelligence, is the key to unlocking our potential. – Winston Churchill"; and Donald J. Trump's 2004 Trump: How to Get Rich printed the quotation credited to Winston Churchill at quote page 77.

Richard Langworth's "Quotes Churchill Never Said" list, part 1, includes under the heading Effort: "Continuous effort—not strength or intelligence—is the key to unlocking our potential. • No attribution."

Richard Langworth's "Quotes Churchill Never Said" list, part 3, includes under the heading Persistence: "Continuous effort—not strength or intelligence—is the key to unlocking our potential. • No attribution. Reported August 2008 in Investor's Business Daily."

The International Churchill Society's Finest Hour 141 article "Red Herrings: Famous Quotes Churchill Never Said" lists "Continuous effort is the key to unlocking our potential." followed by "No attribution found."

The Internet Archive holds a scanned copy of Liane Cordes's The Reflecting Pond: Meditations for Self-Discovery, a 1988 Harper & Row (Harper/Hazelden) printing whose catalogue record states: "Reprint. Originally published: Center City, MN : Hazelden, 1981."
Open Library's record for The Reflecting Pond gives publish date 1981, publisher Hazelden, publish place Center City, MN, 140 pages, ISBN 0894861212.
Wikiquote's Winston Churchill page lists this quotation in its Disputed or Misattributed sections.
